6. Common in parts of the Caribbean and sub-Saharan Africa, the female of this species burrows directly into the skin, typically targeting the areas around the feet or toenails. Once embedded, she feeds on blood and undergoes a dramatic physical transformation, swelling to nearly 7 millimeters in diameter as she fills with eggs. The resulting condition, known as Tuniasis, often requires physical extraction of the insect. Identify it.
